subject.title: Subagent lifecycle observability + async supervision controls

question: Which core contract should own durable subagent lifecycle receipts and audited cancel/steer/resume supervision: the task ledger, the audit ledger, or a dedicated subagent lifecycle API?
rationale: The remaining work is not a mechanical bug fix; it defines persistent state, public gateway protocol, operator permissions, redaction, retention, and security audit semantics.

options.title: Extend task/audit ledgers
options.body: Add subagent lifecycle events and supervision receipts to the existing task and audit surfaces so operators get one public timeline model instead of a new parallel API.

options.title: Create a dedicated subagent lifecycle API
options.body: Introduce a separate SQLite-backed lifecycle ledger and gateway API when task/audit summaries cannot express the required ordered receipt and action semantics cleanly.

options.title: Defer richer supervision receipts
options.body: Keep current summaries and internal controls while closing or narrowing this issue to channel-specific liveness/status work.

recommendation.title: Extend task/audit ledgers
recommendation.body: Add subagent lifecycle events and supervision receipts to the existing task and audit surfaces so operators get one public timeline model instead of a new parallel API.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent and historical trail across subagent lifecycle, registry, announce, and control code that the decision would reshape.
